1. RA 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012,
is the main law in the Philippines aimed at addressing crimes that
involve computer systems. It modernized the legal system to
recognize digital crimes it protected citizens, businesses, and
government against evolving cyber threats.

And aligned the
Philippines with global standards in fighting cybercrime . For me, it
is still effective even in current times because it is continually being
improved and enforced. And it is still recognized by main
corporations, therefore it helps protect our country from criminal
acts caused by computer devices, as our country is known
worldwide for producing malware that spreads across the world,
named as the I Love You virus. 2. Cross-border crime is challenging because cyber criminals can
operate anywhere in the world, which has Different Legal systems,
so what is considered illegal things they are doing in their country
might not necessarily mean it is illegal in the country where they
are operating. Law enforcement authority usually ends at national
borders. So, local authorities' power is out of bounds when the
case is traced back to other countries. To strengthen the fight
against these issues, governments must head towards
globalization with this in mind. Having more international
organizations that fight against crimes like this. An international
agency that is active in solving crimes like this may be beneficial
for the whole world as we head towards advancing through
technology.
